data.narrative:
Dragonfly Aerospace is a Series G stage company in Space & Aerospace that has raised $20M to date. The valuation landscape includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers spanning similar technology and market exposure, though the immediate peer set at Series G lacks sufficient density for robust median benchmarking.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method. Using total capital raised ($20M) as a valuation proxy, the analysis applies a 1.25x multiplier typical for Series G advancement, yielding $51M. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be applied without disclosed revenue; the Space & Aerospace median P/S stands at 27.4x across the 5 public tickers, but application requires target financials. A peer-median approach was rejected due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables (zero same-stage, one adjacent-stage datapoint; minimum threshold is three).

The triangulated range is $44M to $59M, with a median of $51M. This reflects meaningful uncertainty: the analysis rests on a single methodological pillar (stage progression), and the absence of revenue data precludes sector multiple anchoring. Key sensitivities include Dragonfly's unit economics relative to public-market peers and the trajectory of future capital raises. Further refinement would require disclosed or modeled revenue and operational milestones specific to this Series G cohort.
